title: Evaluation of a School Program Helping Children Understand Mental Health
official: Mixed-methods Evaluation of the Intervention "Your Mental Health Matters" on Schoolchildren's Mental Health Literacy
summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to evaluate the effectiveness of a school-based program aimed at increasing mental health literacy in children aged 8 to 12 years, before implemention in French schools. The main question it aims to answer is: "How can we intervene to improve the mental health literacy of children aged 8 to 12?". The outcome measures are: 1) Change in children's mental health literacy score after the school-based intervention; and 2) Change in children's mental health literacy score after the intervention, according to the schools' geographical and socio-economic areas.

Through a mixed-methods approach, researchers will compare the score level of mental health literacy between an intervention and a control group of children with a quasi-experimental cluster trial. The intervention will last 6 weeks (one session of the program per week) during which a teacher and a child psychologist will present mental health according to the theoretical Child-focused Mental Health Literacy Model. Both groups will anser to a questionnaire including the CHILD-MHL scale on child mental health literacy. Additional interviews with teachers and in-class discussion with children will be performed.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Being between 8 and 12 years.
* Being registered in the last two years in French elementary school.
* Belonging to one school from these three areas: urban, rural, and priority education.
